newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends down in spot, fwd on dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends down in spot, fwd on dlr demand.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Monday at 35.795/805 per dollar, down from opening quotes of 35.76/77 on good deamnd for the U.S. currency, dealers said.
They said there was strong dollar demand from corporates and financial institutions.
The rupee traded a a high of 35.7675 and a low of 35.8050 on Monday, deales said.

"There was good buying...it looks like corporate demand," said a dealer at a private bank. "Among the major buyers today were financial institutions, an oil company and one of the country's leading private sector firms. The State Bank of India was also buying," he said.
Dealers said they expected the rupee to drop below 35.80 and could touch 35.85 in the next two days if Monday's dollar demand persisted.
"Otherwise, it will be the old story all over again...the rupee falls briefly but recovers as demand peters out," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Dollar supply still remains good."
Dealers said forward premiums moved up slightly.

"There was some demand for far-forward deliveries...beyond December," said a dealer. "I think premiums had fallen to unrealistic levels and some players may have decided it is the right time to book forward."

"Most of the receiving (of premiums by selling forward dollars) in recent times was speculative," said another dealer. "The market is over-received and there was bound to be a spike in premiums sonner or later."
The annualised premium for six-month dollars ended Monday at 3.63 percent against the weekend close of 3.4 percent.
